thread:
alex.support: heads-up — customer finmetrics reported severe latency and occasional timeouts hitting API from APAC since ~02:40 UTC. p95 ~360ms, p99 ~1.2s on our dashboards, errors 502/504. ticket #4242. escalating for network/edge triage.
maya.sre: looking now. I see a correlated spike across apac-pop-1 and apac-pop-3. Span breakdown shows TLS handshake time ballooning, not tokenization/compute.
kevin.net: running quick probes from our external healthchecks and from a repro VM in ap-southeast: here's traceroute/dig outputs —
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.ai @gslb1.apac.provider
203.0.113.45
203.0.113.46

$ traceroute -n 203.0.113.45
 1  10.10.10.1  1.0 ms  1.1 ms  1.0 ms
 2  198.51.100.5  10.2 ms 10.3 ms 10.1 ms
 3  203.0.113.1  45.0 ms 44.9 ms 44.8 ms
 4  198.51.100.20  120.1 ms 119.8 ms 120.0 ms
 5  93.184.216.34  240.5 ms 241.0 ms 240.8 ms  <-- hairpin to EU backbone
```
kevin.net: traceroute shows an extra cross-region hop (APAC->EU) which explains handshake RTT increase. GSLB is returning APAC answers that actually route via an EU POP (provider-side routing flap).
maya.sre: confirms; TCP/TLS traces show SYN->ACK delay consistent with that hop. Also seeing increased TCP retransmits on those clients.
lia.pm: customer is sensitive (payment flows). support wants a mitigation ASAP, they are asking for either failover to EU or a temporary route change.
kevin.net: I can try to force a different Anycast/POP weight in the GSLB to avoid the misrouted APAC POP. Suggest lowering weight for apac-pop-1 and raising apac-pop-2/backups.
maya.sre: agree. immediate mitigations: 1) reduce GSLB TTL to 30s for impacted prefix 2) adjust weights to shift traffic away from apac-pop-1 3) kick a healthcheck to provider for apac-pop-1 4) enable increased retry backoff in edge for 30 minutes. I'll implement steps 1-3 now.
ops-bot: gslb/config-change: {author: maya.sre, change: "weight apac-pop-1 -> 5, apac-pop-2 -> 95, ttl 30s", change_id: gslb-2904567950} :gear:
maya.sre: pushed the weight change and lowered TTL. also triggered active healthcheck.
deploy-bot: route-policy update deployed (gslb-weights) by maya.sre at 2904567960 — rollout started.
kevin.net: ran a follow-up traceroute after the weight change, now traffic hits apac-pop-2 and stays local:
```
$ traceroute -n 203.0.113.46
 1  10.10.10.1  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.0 ms
 2  198.51.100.6  8.0 ms  8.1 ms  8.0 ms
 3  203.0.113.46  12.5 ms 12.3 ms 12.4 ms
```
maya.sre: metrics look better already — p95 down to ~70ms, p99 down to ~180ms in apac-pop aggregate. retransmits reduced.
lia.pm: relaying to customer: "we've applied an emergency routing change and are monitoring; we expect latency to normalize in the next few minutes."
alex.support: customer reports improved response times on their side, previously timeouts gone. thanks. :tada:
maya.sre: next steps: open follow-up with provider about why apac-pop-1 originated a cross-region egress (probable provider-side backbone failover or BGP mis-origin). collect packet captures + timeline. schedule postmortem.
kevin.net: capturing pcap and BGP dumps now and will hand to provider ops.
ops-bot: incident-note created: incidents/INC-4242-gslb-apac-handoff-latency (owner: maya.sre)
maya.sre: I'll also add a temporary circuit rule to prevent automatic fallback to that provider route until provider confirms fix.
deploy-bot: rollback plan staged: gslb-weights-rollback ready if regressions happen.
alex.support: closing ticket with customer for now; will reopen if regressions. thanks team. :thumbsup:
maya.sre: follow-up postmortem will contain: timeline, repro (dig/traceroute), provider contact thread, and recommended long-term mitigations (healthcheck hardening, provider SLA ask, extended multi-pop replication).
lia.pm: noted — will track PM follow-up and customer comms.
